newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Tenneco asset deal may be hard - AGL.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Tenneco asset deal may be hard - AGL.

text.p: Australia Gas Light Co said on Friday it may not be able to reach an agreement with Tenneco Inc over the sale of Tenneco's Australian assets.
"They might not like some of our terms," AGL managing director Len Bleasel told reporters.
He said AGL would need to know that it could take more of a role than just that of a passive investor.

AGL has previously said it was interested in looking at the Australian assets of Tenneco if they were put up for sale. Tenneco has announced a restructure that includes a proposed merger of its energy arm with El Paso Energy Corp.

Tenneco's Australian assets include the 1700 km of pipeline in South Australia including the state's primary gas pipeline from Moomba to the Adelaide pipeline system. Tenneco is also building a 760 km gas pipeline in southwest Queensland.
Bleasel said AGL's minimum condition was not necessarily that of manager of the assets, although AGL would look for day to day control of the pipeline.

Bleasel also repeated earlier remarks that AGL is on track to at least match its 1995/96 profit in the year ended June 30, 1997. AGL reported a 32 percent rise in net profit to A$124.3 million in 1995/96.

Sales were running ahead of budget so far, Bleasel said, repeating comments he made last month at the annual meeting when he said sales rose two percent in the three months to September 30 compared with a year ago.
Bleasel said AGL was open to other possible acquisitions in Australia's energy sector if the acquisitions enabled the company to gain a dominant role in a particular market.
AGL shares were five cents firmer at A$7.10 at 2.35 p.m. (0335 GMT).
